column1: # sample: GIA sample 1110, synthetic Czochralski ruby (St Gobain, boule SS75), Cr3+ chromophore wafer, plane parallel to c, SIMS-analysed
# host: corundum (Al2O3), uniaxial; E_perp_c = o-ray, E_par_c = e-ray

# composition: Cr 134 ppma +- 7.6 % of all atoms (SIMS) = 1.58e19 cm^-3 = 0.050 wt% Cr2O3 = 3.35e-4 Cr/(Al+Cr); high-purity, no numeric Fe or Ti value; the link between this wafer and the quoted Cr value is ~90 % likely

# units: lambda_nm; absorption cross section sigma in cm^2 per Cr3+ ion, Napierian, reflection-corrected (alpha = sigma N, T = exp(-sigma N L)); 1 nm grid, 1.5 nm resolution, 200-800 nm of the 200-1100 nm sheet; a flat floor of ~1.5e-21 cm^2 at 640-800 nm is instrument baseline
# path_cm: not applicable (sigma is thickness independent; the wafer thickness is not stated)

# source: Dubinsky, Stone-Sundberg & Emmett 2020, Gems & Gemology 56(1) 2-28, absorption cross-section data sheet sp20-corundum-chromophores-absorption-cross-section-data.xlsx (column Cr3+ sigma, E perp c / E par c), via docs/chromophores/primary-2026-10/data/ruby/GIA_Dubinsky2020_sample1110_Cr3+_cross_section_200-800nm.csv; wavelengths sorted ascending, values unchanged; research-2026-10-primary-data.md section 2.1

# note: no measured color exists; the appendix2_lab lines are GIA Appendix 2 CALCULATED L*a*b* (illuminant A 2856 K and D65, 2 degree observer, Lab vs the illuminant white) at the areal density in ppma*cm (1 ppma of all atoms = 1.178e17 cm^-3); 'both' is the unpolarised mix (2 E_perp_c + E_par_c) / 3; the spectrum multiplier column of Appendix 2 is internally inconsistent and unused
